title: U.S. Senate · Mississippi

context.text: This is the Class II Senate seat held by Cindy Hyde-Smith, who first took office in 2018. Hyde-Smith defeated Sarah Adlakha in the March 10, 2026 Republican primary, 80.8% to 19.2%. Scott Colom defeated Priscilla W. Till and Albert Littell in the Democratic primary, 72.9% to 18.6% to 8.5%. Ty Pinkins is running as an independent.

summary.text: Cindy Hyde-Smith is the incumbent U.S. Senator from Mississippi, appointed in 2018 to fill Thad Cochran's seat, elected to complete his term later that year, and elected to a full term in 2020. She previously served as Mississippi Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce (2012-2018) and in the Mississippi State Senate (2000-2012).

background.text: Served in the Mississippi State Senate representing District 39 from 2000 to 2012.
Served as Mississippi Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce from 2012 to 2018.
Appointed to the U.S. Senate by Gov. Phil Bryant in 2018 to fill the seat of Thad Cochran, then won a special election that November and a full term in 2020.
Is a cattle farmer by profession.

priorities.text: Supports federal policies to foster economic growth and job creation in Mississippi, including the 2017 tax cuts.
Supports the state's agriculture and forestry industries, citing her background as a cattle farmer and former state agriculture commissioner.

positions.summary: Her Senate issues page says she believes the Affordable Care Act should be repealed.
positions.quote: She believes the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, better known as Obamacare, should be repealed.

positions.summary: Her Senate issues page says she is committed to supporting policies and legislation to protect the lives of unborn children and has a record of opposing measures that encourage abortion.
positions.quote: She is committed to supporting policies and legislation to protect the lives of unborn children.

positions.summary: Cosponsored S. 128, the SAVE Act, which requires documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.
Cosponsored S. 9, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act of 2025, which would bar transgender women and girls from women's and girls' school sports.

candidates.name: Scott Colom
candidates.currentRole: District Attorney, Mississippi 16th Circuit Court District

summary.text: Scott Colom is the elected District Attorney for Mississippi's 16th Circuit Court District (Clay, Lowndes, Noxubee, and Oktibbeha counties). He was twice nominated by President Biden to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi, but his nomination was not confirmed by the Senate. He is running for U.S. Senate as the Democratic nominee.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Millsaps College (2005) and a law degree from the University of Wisconsin Law School (2009).
Elected District Attorney for Mississippi's 16th Circuit Court District.
Nominated by President Biden to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi in 2022 and again in 2023; the nomination was not acted on by the Senate and lapsed.
Describes himself as a seventh-generation Mississippian; his mother, Dorothy Colom, was the first African American elected to her region's Chancery Court.

priorities.text: Says he is running to lower costs for Mississippi families.
Says he wants to save Mississippi's rural hospitals.
Says he wants to bring jobs home to Mississippi.

positions.summary: In a Starkville Daily News Q&A he called for restoring the expired health insurance tax credits and reversing Medicaid cuts.
positions.quote: restore the tax credits that helped working people afford coverage, and reverse the Medicaid cuts that put eight rural hospitals at risk of closing

positions.summary: In a Starkville Daily News Q&A he said he opposes the SAVE Act's documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement.
positions.quote: The problem is the SAVE Act is different — it requires documentary proof of citizenship, and I oppose that.

positions.summary: In the same Q&A he said raising the minimum wage is long overdue.
positions.quote: Raising the minimum wage is long overdue

positions.summary: In the same Q&A he called for asking the highest earners to pay Social Security payroll tax on income above the current cap.
positions.quote: We should ask the highest earners to contribute their part.

summary.text: Ty Pinkins is a Mississippi attorney and U.S. Army veteran (21 years of service, including three combat tours) running as an independent for U.S. Senate. He previously ran for U.S. Senate as a Democrat in 2024 and for Mississippi Secretary of State in 2023.

background.text: Born and raised in Rolling Fork, Mississippi.
Served 21 years in the U.S. Army, including three combat tours, and served as a White House Communications Aide.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Maryland Global Campus (2012), a J.D. from Georgetown University Law Center (2020), and an LL.M. in national security law from Georgetown (2021).
Has worked as an attorney with the Mississippi Center for Justice.

priorities.text: Says the two-party system has "stopped working for too many Americans" and is running as an independent so Mississippi has "a senator who answers to the people, not party bosses or political establishments."
priorities.quote: Both major parties have failed working people. My campaign is rooted in the belief that the two-party system has stopped working for too many Americans.

priorities.text: Says he is passionate about expanding access to affordable healthcare, especially in rural areas.
Says he wants to ensure veterans receive the benefits, care, and support they earned.

positions.summary: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey lists expanding access to affordable healthcare, especially in rural areas, as a passion.
